# Data quality rule catalogue

76 row-level rules across 7 datasets, plus 27 warehouse-level checks.

**Severity**

| Severity | Effect |
|---|---|
| `reject` | The row is written to quarantine with its rule ids and error messages; it never reaches silver. |
| `warn` | The row is kept; the rule id is appended to its `quality_warnings` array and counted in `monitoring.quality_results`. |

**Check types**

| Check | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `not_null` | value must be present |
| `regex` | value must match a pattern |
| `in_set` | value must be one of an allowed set |
| `castable` | the raw string must convert to the target type |
| `compare` | value compared against a constant |
| `compare_cols` | two columns compared |
| `not_future` | timestamp must not be after the reference timestamp |
| `fk` | value must exist in a reference dataset |
| `expr` | arbitrary SQL boolean expression |

Columns suffixed `_t` are typed casts of the raw string and `_n` are normalised strings, both computed by the silver job before validation.

## Circuit breakers (max reject rate per dataset)

| Dataset | Max reject rate | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| `customers` | 5% | primary dataset - a higher rate means the source is broken |
| `products` | 5% | primary dataset - a higher rate means the source is broken |
| `orders` | 5% | primary dataset - a higher rate means the source is broken |
| `order_items` | 10% | child dataset - inherits rejections from its parent, so the budget is wider |
| `payments` | 10% | child dataset - inherits rejections from its parent, so the budget is wider |
| `inventory_events` | 5% | primary dataset - a higher rate means the source is broken |
| `shipping_events` | 10% | child dataset - inherits rejections from its parent, so the budget is wider |

Exceeding the rate raises `QualityThresholdError` and aborts the run before anything is published.

## `customers`

Customer master from the CRM export.

| Rule id | Severity | Check | Column | Rule | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `customers.customer_id_not_null` | reject | `not_null` | `customer_id` | customer_id is required | Primary business key; rows without it cannot be matched to orders. |
| `customers.customer_id_format` | reject | `regex` | `customer_id` | customer_id must look like CUST-000000 `^CUST-\d{6}$` | - |
| `customers.email_format` | warn | `regex` | `email_n` | email is not a valid address (set to NULL) `^[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}$` | A bad contact field must not erase the customer's order history; the value is nulled and reported. |
| `customers.email_present` | warn | `not_null` | `email_n` | email is missing | - |
| `customers.signup_date_valid` | warn | `castable` | `signup_date` | signup_date is not a valid date (set to NULL) | - |
| `customers.signup_date_not_future` | warn | `not_future` | `signup_date_t` | signup_date is in the future (set to NULL) | - |
| `customers.updated_at_valid` | reject | `castable` | `updated_at` | updated_at must be a valid timestamp | - |
| `customers.segment_allowed` | reject | `in_set` | `customer_segment_n` | customer_segment must be consumer|business|vip `consumer`, `business`, `vip` | - |
| `customers.region_known` | reject | `fk` | `region_code` | region_code must exist in the regions reference -> `regions.region_code` | - |
| `customers.country_recognised` | warn | `not_null` | `country_code_n` | country could not be mapped to an ISO code | Unknown spellings are kept (country_code NULL) and reported so the alias map can be extended. |
| `customers.birth_date_valid` | warn | `castable` | `birth_date` | birth_date is not a valid date (set to NULL) | - |
